introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Physics, Paper 2 (subject code 0580). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**EITHER 9 (a), (b) and (c)**

Define the following and state their S.I. units of measurement.

(i) Heat. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Temperature. *[2 marks]*

(iii) State two features on a clinical thermometer that makes it different from a normal liquid-in-glass thermometer. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Heat** is the energy transferred from a hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature. SI unit: the **joule (J)**.

(ii) **Temperature** is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body (it measures the average kinetic energy of its molecules and decides the direction in which heat flows). SI unit: the **kelvin (K)**.

(iii) 1. It has a **constriction** (narrow kink) in the tube just above the bulb, which stops the mercury from flowing back so that the reading stays after the thermometer is removed from the body.
2. It has a **short, narrow range** (about $35\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $42\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) with a finer scale, covering only body temperatures.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Distinguish between heat capacity and specific heat capacity. *[2 marks]*

(ii) $500\,\mathrm{g}$ of water were heated using an electric heater rated $1000\,\mathrm{W}$ for $2$ minutes. If the specific heat capacity of water is $4200\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, calculate the temperature change. *[4 marks]*

(iii) State one use of water due to its high specific heat capacity. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Heat capacity** is the quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of a given body (the whole object) by $1\,\mathrm{K}$; unit $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. **Specific heat capacity** is the quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ of a substance by $1\,\mathrm{K}$; unit $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

(ii) Energy supplied by the heater: $Q = Pt = 1000\times(2\times 60) = 120\,000\,\mathrm{J}$.

Assuming that all this energy is absorbed by the water: $Q = mc\Delta\theta$, with $m = 500\,\mathrm{g} = 0.5\,\mathrm{kg}$.

$\Delta\theta = \dfrac{Q}{mc} = \dfrac{120\,000}{0.5\times 4200} = \dfrac{120\,000}{2100} \approx 57\,\mathrm{K}$ (that is $57\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$).

(iii) Water is used as a **coolant** (for example in a car radiator) or in a hot-water bottle or central-heating system, because it can absorb or store a lot of heat for a small rise in temperature.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define thermal expansion. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Explain how a bimetallic strip works in an electric iron to switch it on and off. *[3 marks]*

(iii) Explain why a metal spoon, left beside a flame for a few minutes becomes so hot to touch. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Thermal expansion** is the increase in the length, area or volume of a substance when its temperature rises.

(ii) A bimetallic strip is made of two different metals (for example brass and iron) firmly joined together. When heated, the two metals expand by **different amounts** (brass expands more than iron), so the strip **bends** towards the metal that expands less. In the iron, the strip is part of the circuit of the heating element: when the iron reaches the set temperature the strip bends enough to **break the contact** and the heater is switched off. When the iron cools, the strip straightens, the contacts close again and the heater is switched on. The temperature setting is changed by a control knob that moves the contact.

(iii) Metals are **good conductors of heat**. The part of the spoon near the flame is heated; its atoms vibrate more and the free electrons carry the energy rapidly along the metal by **conduction** to the other end, so the whole spoon, including the handle, soon becomes hot.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**OR 9 (d), (e) and (f)**

Define the following:

(i) Radioactivity. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Half-life. *[2 marks]*

(iii) State two differences between n-type and p-type semiconductors. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Radioactivity** is the spontaneous disintegration (decay) of unstable atomic nuclei, with the emission of alpha particles, beta particles or gamma rays.

(ii) **Half-life** is the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay (equivalently, for the activity of the sample to fall to half its value).

(iii) 1. An **n-type** semiconductor is made by doping with a **pentavalent** impurity (e.g. phosphorus, arsenic), a **p-type** by doping with a **trivalent** impurity (e.g. boron, aluminium).
2. In n-type the majority charge carriers are **free electrons** (negative); in p-type the majority carriers are **holes** (positive).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Distinguish between fusion and fission. *[2 marks]*

In a radioactive fission reaction, a nuclide ${}^{238}_{92}X$ undergoes two $\alpha$-decays and two $\beta$-decays to form a daughter nuclide.

(ii) Write a balanced equation for this reaction. *[4 marks]*

(iii) State one use of a named radioisotope. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Fusion:** two light nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus with release of energy (it needs extremely high temperature, as in the Sun). **Fission:** a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei (usually after absorbing a neutron), releasing energy and neutrons.

(ii) Each $\alpha$-decay removes $4$ from the mass number and $2$ from the atomic number; each $\beta$-decay raises the atomic number by $1$ and leaves the mass number unchanged.

Mass number: $238 - 2\times 4 = 230$. Atomic number: $92 - 2\times 2 + 2\times 1 = 90$.

$${}^{238}_{92}X \rightarrow {}^{230}_{90}Y + 2\,{}^{4}_{2}\mathrm{He} + 2\,{}^{0}_{-1}e$$

Check: mass numbers $238 = 230 + 8 + 0$; charges $92 = 90 + 4 - 2$. The daughter nuclide ${}^{230}_{90}Y$ is thorium-230 (the parent X is uranium-238); the antineutrinos emitted with the $\beta$ particles are left out.

(iii) Examples: **cobalt-60** is used in radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells (or to sterilise medical equipment); **carbon-14** is used to date old organic objects; **iodine-131** is used as a tracer in the thyroid gland.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define background radiation. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State and explain the nature of tracks produced by alpha particles in a cloud chamber. *[3 marks]*

(iii) State two safety precautions to take in handling radioactive materials. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Background radiation** is the ionising radiation that is always present around us, coming from natural sources (cosmic rays, radioactive rocks and soil, radon gas in the air, food and water) and from artificial sources (e.g. medical X-rays).

(ii) Alpha particles leave **short, thick, straight tracks**. They are heavy and strongly ionising, so they ionise many air molecules along their path, and the vapour condenses on these ions to form a dense, bright trail; they lose their energy quickly and so travel only a few centimetres; being heavy they are hardly deflected, so the tracks are straight.

(iii) 1. Handle sources with **tongs** (never with bare hands) and keep them as far from the body as possible.
2. Store the sources in **lead-lined containers** and keep the time of exposure short; wear protective clothing and a film badge, and do not eat or drink where the sources are used.
